attributes.body:
Coming from the こそあど言葉（ことば） family of words, こう, そう, ああ, or どう may be used with the verb 言（い）う to form an expression which literally means 'in the way of (A)'. (A) being 'this' これ, 'that' それ, 'that over there' あれ, or 'what' どれ (in questions). As with all pre-noun adjectival words, this expression will be used directly before a noun.

Although こう, そう, ああ, and どう share a relationship with これ, それ, あれ, and どれ, they are their own individual words, which each have a meaning similar to 'as such'. These words are all adverb when used by themselves.

Caution

そう (the adverb), should not be confused with そう, the auxiliary verb. そう (the adverb) comes from the kanji 然（そ）う, while the auxiliary verb does not have a kanji form.

そういう (and its variants こういう, ああいう, どういう) and そんな・こんな・あんな・どんな both modify nouns to mean 'that sort of,' 'this sort of,' etc. While often similar in meaning, そういう tends to be a bit more formal or polite. In contrast, depending on context そんな can be used with a negative or dismissive tone, which is not true of そういう.
